questions.stem: Agents and managers cannot create knowledge articles from Community questions.
questions.explanation: False. Agents and managers CAN create knowledge articles from Community questions. The sn_customerservice_manager role includes knowledge capabilities, and agents with the knowledge role (contained in sn_customerservice_agent) can create articles. Community questions can be converted to knowledge articles to capture and share solutions.

questions.stem: Information about a customer’s service contract is found in Knowledge.
questions.explanation: False. Information about a customer's service contract is found in Service Contracts and Entitlements, not in Knowledge. Knowledge bases contain articles with solutions, FAQs, and product information. Contract details such as service levels, terms, and entitlement specifics are stored in the Customer Contracts and Entitlements module.

questions.stem: From what places in SN can an agent create a case? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Agents can create cases from the Customer Service Application (A), from an Account record (C), and from Chat (D). The Customer Service Application provides the primary interface for case creation. Account records have related links to create cases for that account. Chat interactions can be converted to cases. Contact records (B) don't provide a direct case creation option OOB.

questions.stem: What are the conditions that matching rules are based on? (Choose two.)

options.text: Agent resources best suited to work on a case
Filters set up in advanced work assignment

questions.explanation: Matching rules are based on conditions related to agent resources best suited to work on a case (A) and specific case attributes (D). Matching rules evaluate agent capabilities (skills, availability, workload) against case attributes (category, priority, product) to find the best match. Routing rules (B) are separate from matching. Filters in AWA (C) are not what matching conditions are based on.

questions.stem: Matching rules enhance assignment capability by ____________________.

options.text: Providing dynamic matching of cases to groups or individuals
Determining if account is a customer or partner

questions.explanation: Matching rules enhance assignment capability by matching the best agent by availability. While matching rules also evaluate skills and other criteria, the core enhancement they provide is dynamically identifying agents who are currently available. Option B describes the broader AWA functionality. Options C and D don't describe matching rule enhancements.

questions.stem: Special Handling Notes can apply to which one of the following based on specific attributes?
questions.explanation: Special Handling Notes can apply to a Contact based on specific attributes. Out of the box, SHN can be applied based on Contact, Account, and Product. Among the given options, Contact (B) is the correct answer. Domain (A), Holiday (C), and VIP (D) are not entities that SHN applies to directly.

questions.stem: Predictive Intelligence improves Case management by:

options.text: Predicting what values should have gone into empty fields in historical records
Reducing the number of records needed to accurately predict a value
Predicting Case values without manual intervention

questions.explanation: Predictive Intelligence improves Case management by predicting case values without manual intervention. It uses machine learning to automatically populate fields like Category, Priority, and Assignment Group based on case data patterns. It doesn't predict values for empty historical fields (A), doesn't reduce required training records (B), and doesn't replace routing rules (C).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a condition for matching rules?
questions.explanation: Specific case attributes (D) is a condition for matching rules. Matching rules evaluate case attributes such as category, product, priority, and other case-specific fields to determine appropriate agent assignment. Agent domain (A), Assignment (B), and Switching (C) are not matching rule conditions.

questions.stem: What do blue circles in the timeline of a case form represent?
questions.explanation: Blue circles in the timeline of a case form represent State changes. The case timeline visually tracks the progression of a case through its lifecycle states (New, Open, Awaiting Info, Resolved, Closed) using blue circle indicators. Notes (A), Activities (C), and Comments (D) use different visual indicators in the timeline.

questions.stem: Predictive Intelligence improves triage quality by eliminating the guesswork. Predictive Intelligence supports which of the following decisions? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Predictive Intelligence supports Case Categorization (C) and Case Prioritization (D) decisions. These are the two primary triage decisions that PI automates by analyzing historical data patterns to predict the correct category and priority for new cases. Case Escalation (A) and Case State (B) are not PI-supported prediction decisions.

questions.stem: Which Business Rules are part of the Customer Service Management baseline configuration? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Auto Assessment (B) and Update Case Entitlement (D) are business rules in the CSM baseline configuration. Auto Assessment automatically triggers assessment evaluations. Update Case Entitlement ensures entitlements are properly linked when case attributes change. Apply Role by Customer (A) and Change Update to Close (C) are not standard CSM baseline business rules.

questions.stem: What are the Critical Success Factors that are related to CSM Suite Implementations? (Choose four.)

options.text: Have a clear understanding of the use cases
Define the number of hours needed to develop the associated requirements
Implementation is only as good as the underlying process

questions.explanation: Critical Success Factors for CSM implementations include: Define Business Pain Points (A), Provide consistent service (B), Have clear understanding of use cases (C), and Implementation is only as good as the underlying process (E). Defining hours needed for development (D) is a project planning task, not a critical success factor for ensuring implementation quality.

questions.stem: What should be emphasized when designing solutions? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: When designing solutions, emphasize: Minimize customizations (A), Focus on Out-of-the-box functionality (B), and Design for Scalability (C). These three principles ensure sustainable, upgradeable implementations. Mobile-friendly functionality (D) is a feature consideration, not a core design principle for solution architecture.

questions.stem: What role does the Engagement Manager play before the Workshop? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Before the Workshop, the Engagement Manager plays the role of Project Manager (A) and Assists with technical requirements (D). The Engagement Manager leads pre-workshop preparation including project planning and gathering technical requirements. Acting as intermediary (B) and providing technical answers (C) are not the Engagement Manager's pre-workshop responsibilities.

questions.stem: What should be part of the pre-engagement collateral?

options.text: Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) and pricing sheet

questions.explanation: The Scoping Guide should be part of the pre-engagement collateral. It helps define project scope, requirements, and boundaries before the engagement begins. FAQ (A) is general information, not pre-engagement material. Roles template (C) and SKU/pricing (D) are operational documents, not standard pre-engagement collateral items.

questions.stem: Articles can provide the following: (Choose three.)

options.text: Provide answers and responses to common issues or questions

questions.explanation: Knowledge articles provide: Document current and known issues (A), Provide answers to common questions (B), and Share product information (D). These align with KCS best practices for knowledge content. Information about customer service contracts (C) is stored in Entitlements/Contracts, not Knowledge articles.

questions.stem: Contextual Search framework is used for providing Knowledge search results in which of these scenarios?

options.text: Both portal question entry and Record Producer

questions.explanation: The Contextual Search framework provides Knowledge search results in both portal question entry and Record Producer scenarios. Contextual Search dynamically suggests relevant knowledge articles based on text entered by users, whether they are filling out a portal form or working with a Record Producer. It serves both contexts, not just one.

questions.stem: Which of the following are true regarding integrating a ServiceNow Knowledge base with external content? (Choose two.)

options.text: Imported external articles appear as attachments in ServiceNow
Only applications that allow WebDAV connections can be integrated
The imported article will have the same category it had in the source knowledge base

questions.explanation: When integrating a ServiceNow Knowledge base with external content: imported external articles appear as attachments in ServiceNow (A), and only applications that allow WebDAV connections can be integrated (B). External articles retain their format as attachments. The WebDAV protocol requirement means not all external systems can integrate. Categories aren't preserved (C), and SharePoint supports this integration (D).

questions.stem: Access to a Knowledge base or Article can be restricted based on a customer’s assets and the product models using which of the following? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Knowledge base/article access can be restricted based on customer assets and product models using Knowledge Product Entitlements (A) and User Criteria (D). Knowledge Product Entitlements restrict access based on products owned, while User Criteria provides granular access control based on user attributes. Data Policy (B) controls field behavior. ACLs (C) are lower-level security, not the primary mechanism for this.

questions.stem: What are some benefits that Knowledge Product Entitlement provide? (Choose three.)

options.text: Makes it easier for Agents to manage case volume
Allows access to Knowledge Articles that are related to products owned by a customer

questions.explanation: Knowledge Product Entitlement benefits: Reduces call volume (A), Makes it easier for agents to manage case volume (B), and Allows access to Knowledge Articles related to products owned by a customer (C). These benefits align with self-service deflection and targeted knowledge delivery. Contract information (D) and marketing (E) are not KPE benefits.

questions.stem: What are the characteristics of Knowledge Categories?

options.text: Shareable across KBs: Yes ; Multi-Level: No
Shareable across KBs: No ; Multi-Level: Yes
Shareable across KBs: No ; Multi-Level: No
Shareable across KBs: Yes ; Multi-Level: Yes

questions.explanation: Knowledge Categories are NOT shareable across knowledge bases (No) but ARE multi-level (Yes). Each knowledge base has its own category hierarchy, and categories can be nested multiple levels deep. Categories are specific to individual knowledge bases and cannot be shared or reused across different knowledge bases.

questions.stem: Users with the sn_customerservice.proxy_contact role can do which of the following? (Choose two.)

options.text: Manage cases on behalf of customer service agents
Create cases on behalf of customers
Manage requests on behalf of customer service agents
Create requests on behalf of customers
Manage major incident communication on behalf of a customer service manager

questions.explanation: Users with the sn_customerservice.proxy_contact role can create cases on behalf of customers (B) and create requests on behalf of customers (D). The proxy_contact role enables internal employees to act on behalf of external customers for both case and request creation, without being assigned customer-facing roles.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a Catalog Item variable?

options.text: Grants the customer the opportunity to ask a question
Opens a wizard to help a customer fill in a case form
Guides a customer by providing hints on case forms
Allows the customer or consumer to qualify their answer

questions.explanation: A Catalog Item variable allows the customer or consumer to qualify their answer by providing specific details. Variables on catalog items are form fields that capture additional information from the requester, helping them specify exactly what they need. Options A (ask a question), B (wizard), and C (hints) don't describe the core purpose of catalog variables.

questions.stem: What one of the following is optional when creating a Catalog workflow?
questions.explanation: Approving the workflow is optional when creating a Catalog workflow. Not all workflows require an approval step — simple fulfillment workflows may proceed directly to task execution. Publishing (A), defining activities (B), and managing versions (D) are required or inherent parts of the workflow creation process.

questions.stem: What module is used to create Case Record Producers?
questions.explanation: Record Producers is the module used to create Case Record Producers. You navigate to Service Catalog > Catalog Definitions > Record Producers to create a new record producer that generates case records. The other options (A, B, D) are not actual ServiceNow module names for creating record producers.

questions.stem: Which one is NOT a dependency for the Customer Service Plugin?
questions.explanation: Communities is NOT a dependency for the Customer Service Plugin. While Communities can integrate with CSM, it's a separate optional application. Task Activities (A), Skills Management (B), and Openframe (C) are all dependencies that get activated when the CSM plugin is installed.

questions.stem: ACME corporation wants to use ServiceNow CSM for supporting their customers through Twitter. What CSM entity would you recommend ACME to store the customer’s Twitter profile details?
questions.explanation: Social Profile is the CSM entity for storing a customer's Twitter profile details. ServiceNow CSM uses Social Profiles to store social media identity information including Twitter handles, Facebook profiles, etc. Account (A) stores company info. Consumer (C) stores individual details. Social Profile specifically links social media identities to CSM records.

questions.stem: Which social media channels are NOT available out-of-box?
questions.explanation: LinkedIn is NOT available out-of-box as a social media channel in CSM. ServiceNow CSM provides OOB integration with Facebook and Twitter for social media case creation and monitoring. LinkedIn integration is not included OOB and would require custom configuration or a third-party integration.

questions.stem: What is the equivalent of NOT selecting any group, when configuring multiple active configurations of OpenFrame?
questions.explanation: Not selecting any group when configuring multiple active OpenFrame configurations is equivalent to selecting all the groups. If no group is specified, the configuration applies to all users/groups, effectively making it a global configuration. This is the default behavior — no group restriction means everyone has access.

questions.stem: How many outbound email accounts are supported in Customer Service Management?
questions.explanation: Only one outbound email account is supported in Customer Service Management. CSM supports a single outgoing email configuration for sending case-related notifications and correspondence. Multiple outbound accounts (B, C, D) are not supported OOB.

questions.stem: What are features of Customer Service Management? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: CSM features include: Service Entitlements (B), Real-time SLAs (E), Service Contracts (F), and Skills-based routing (G). These are core CSM capabilities for managing customer service delivery. Timed Audits (A), Demand Management (C), and Service Prospecting (D) are not CSM features.

questions.stem: What are the Forum User Types? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The Forum User Types are Registered (B), Public (C), and Custom (D). Registered users have accounts and can post. Public users can view content without accounts. Custom types allow administrators to create specialized user categories. Admin (A) and Moderator (E) are roles, not user types.

questions.stem: Which of the following are true regarding the Community Portal application? (Choose two.)

options.text: It is available to any customer with a Community license
It is available by default with the Support and Service portals
It is only available to CSM license holders
Most of the configuration does not require System Administrator role

questions.explanation: The Community Portal application is available to any customer with a Community license (A), and most of the configuration does not require System Administrator role (D). It's not limited to CSM license holders (C) and is not available by default with Support/Service portals (B) — it requires its own license.

questions.stem: If only one user reports a content for moderation, the content will be hidden.
questions.explanation: False. If only one user reports content for moderation, the content will NOT be hidden automatically. Content moderation typically requires a threshold of reports or moderator review before content is hidden. A single report triggers a review process but doesn't automatically hide the content.

questions.stem: The available case types are: (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The available case types in CSM are Order (B) and Product (C). These are the two case types provided when the CSM Demo Data plugin is activated. Product cases handle product-related issues, while Order cases handle order-related issues. Product Support (A) and Support (D) are not OOB case types.

questions.stem: What is required to enable the Follow the sun field on the Customer Service Case form?

options.text: Nothing, it is a standard field
The value property on the form must be set to true
The plugin ‘com.snc.csm_time_recording’ needs to be activated
The value property on the form must be set to true and the field added to the case form

questions.explanation: To enable the Follow the Sun field on the Customer Service Case form, the value property on the form must be set to true AND the field must be added to the case form. Both steps are required — the property enables the functionality and the field must be visible on the form. It's not a standard field by default (A), and the plugin (C) is not required.

questions.stem: In the Customer Service Management space, what does the term asset management mean?

options.text: Financial, contractual and inventory information of assets
A set of business activities and processes used to track assets
Tracking products or services customers are using

questions.explanation: In the CSM space, asset management means tracking products or services customers are using. Unlike ITSM asset management which focuses on financial and lifecycle tracking, CSM uses assets to represent specific product instances deployed for and supported for customers. Options A, B, and C describe ITSM and corporate asset management perspectives.

questions.stem: Which of the following roles cannot update a consumer’s record?
questions.explanation: The sn_customerservice_agent role cannot update a consumer's record. The CSM roles documentation shows that the consumer_agent role (contained in sn_customerservice_manager) is required to work with consumer records. The agent role handles B2B (account/contact) scenarios. sn_customerservice_manager (B), consumer_agent (C), and admin (D) can all update consumer records.

questions.stem: Major Issue Management uses which one of the following capabilities?
questions.explanation: Major Issue Management uses Targeted Communications capability. When a major issue affects multiple customers, targeted communications (publications) enable the organization to proactively notify all impacted customers about the issue, status updates, and resolution progress. GRC (A), Asset management (C), and Record producers (D) are not used by Major Issue Management.

questions.stem: What is required to synchronize fields from a parent to a child case(s)?

options.text: The advanced plugin (com.sns.pa.customer_service_advanced) needs to be activated
Major Issue Management needs to be installed and certain properties enabled
No action required, this is a standard Customer Service Management feature
The role of sn_customerservice.customer_case_manager must be assigned

questions.explanation: Major Issue Management needs to be installed and certain properties enabled to synchronize fields from a parent to child cases. Parent-child case synchronization is a feature of Major Issue Management that allows field updates on the parent case to automatically propagate to associated child cases. It's not a standard CSM feature (C) without MIM.

questions.stem:
HOTSPOT -
Match the definitions for roles relationships.
questions.explanation: This is a HOTSPOT matching question requiring visual interaction. The question asks to match definitions to role relationships. Without the specific drag-and-drop options visible, this is based on CSM role relationship knowledge including Account-Contact, Partner-Customer, and Household-Consumer relationships.

questions.stem: Which of the following functions can be completed when using the Field Service Management Application on a mobile device offline? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: On a mobile device offline with FSM, you can: Execute assigned tasks (B), Close work orders (C), and Manage assets (E). The mobile app caches assigned work for offline use, allowing field technicians to complete tasks, close work orders, and manage asset information. Managing requests (A) and cases (D) require online connectivity to the CSM application.

questions.stem: Information in the Case Field ‘Contact’ is copied to which Incident Field?
questions.explanation: The Contact field on a CSM case is copied to the Caller field on an Incident. When CSM integrates with ITSM and an incident is created from a case, the case Contact maps to the incident Caller field. Both represent the person reporting the issue, but CSM uses 'Contact' while ITSM uses 'Caller' terminology.

questions.stem: How many active OpenFrame configurations can you have on an instance?
questions.explanation: You can have unlimited active OpenFrame configurations on an instance. OpenFrame supports multiple configurations simultaneously, allowing different CTI integrations or channel configurations for different groups of agents. There is no limit on the number of active configurations.

questions.stem: What are common types of application record data that are imported during a CSM data migration? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Common types of application record data imported during CSM data migration include Knowledge Articles (A) and Accounts (B). These are foundational data sets that must be imported to enable the CSM application — accounts represent your customers and knowledge articles support case resolution. Chat (C) and Case (D) data are typically not migrated from legacy systems.

questions.stem: Which are the key self-service functions of the Customer Support Portal? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Key self-service functions of the Customer Support Portal are: Community (A), Knowledge Base (B), and Service Catalog (D). These enable customers to find answers, browse community discussions, and request services without agent assistance. Open An Incident (C) is an ITSM self-service function, not a CSM portal function.

questions.stem: Which of the following are channels? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Web (B) and Chat (C) are communication channels in CSM. Channels represent the methods through which customers interact with support — Web (portal), Chat, Email, Phone, and Social. Contacts (A) are people associated with accounts, not channels. Article (D) is a knowledge content type, not a channel.

questions.stem: Out-of-the-box, the consumer support portal (/csp) CANNOT be used for which one of the following actions?
questions.explanation: Out-of-the-box, the consumer support portal (/csp) CANNOT be used to open an incident. The consumer portal supports viewing knowledge articles (B), live chat (C), and consumer self-registration (D), but incident creation is an ITSM function not available on the consumer service portal.

questions.stem: The Customer Support Portal default configuration provides the following channels to interact with customers? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Customer Support Portal default configuration provides Chat (C) and Email (D) channels for interacting with customers. These are the two interactive communication channels configured by default. Web (A) is how customers access the portal itself, not a communication channel. Social (B) requires additional configuration and plugin activation.

questions.stem:
HOTSPOT -
Match the business rule to its function in the Self-Service Portal.
questions.explanation: Display request message; Display rule; Update account based on reg code; validate_registration. The answer image shows the correct matching of CSM Self-Service Portal business rules: (1) 'After registration request submittal, shows info message to user' matches 'Display request message' — this rule triggers after form submission to show a confirmation. (2) 'Shows message to remind users to enter a correct registration code' matches 'Display rule' — a UI display rule that prompts for valid input. (3) 'Validates registration code and assigns account' matches 'Update account based on reg code' — validates code and links the user account. (4) 'Checks if registration is valid based on email address' matches 'validate_registration' — a validation script that checks email-based registration.

questions.stem: The ServiceNow Communities feature is only available for customers with ServiceNow Customer Services Management licenses.
questions.explanation: False. Communities is a separate application available to any customer with a Community license, not limited to CSM license holders. The Communities feature can be used independently of CSM, though it integrates well with Customer Service Management for knowledge sharing and case deflection.

questions.stem:
Read the use case below to determine if the customer service relationship is B2B or B2C.
Mary Contrary experiences a power outage and call the electrical company. The agent determines the outage is local to the customer and scheduled a technician to Mary’s house.
questions.explanation: This is a B2C (Business-to-Consumer) scenario. Mary is an individual consumer calling the electrical company directly for service. B2C involves a service provider supporting individual customers/consumers rather than businesses. B2B would involve one business supporting another business's employees.

questions.stem: If the CSM Demo Data Plugin has been installed what are two options either of which will prepare that instance to be used as part of the release path to production? (Choose two.)

options.text: Remove the Demo Data via a HI Request
Clone back to this instance from a valid instance

questions.explanation: To prepare an instance with demo data for production release path: Remove the Demo Data via a HI Request (C) or Clone back from a valid instance (D). Demo data must be removed before going to production. Zbooting (A) resets the entire instance. Disabling Case Interceptor (B) doesn't address demo data.

questions.stem: What criteria can be used to determine when a new inbound case should be opened?

options.text: When a new customer is created
When a customer has a question or issue to resolve
When we have new marketing material for a customer

questions.explanation: A new inbound case should be opened when a customer has a question or issue to resolve. Cases in CSM are created to track and manage customer-reported questions, issues, or problems. New customer creation (A), internal problems (B), and marketing materials (D) are not valid triggers for opening a customer service case.

questions.stem:
From a service provider’s perspective, is the following a product or an asset?
A cable modem model that the service provider sells.
questions.explanation: A cable modem model that the service provider sells is a Product. Products represent models/types of items that a company offers. An Asset would be a specific instance of that product deployed to a particular customer. Since this describes the model being sold (not a specific unit in use), it's a Product.

questions.stem: Entitlements specify the level of service provided to customers.
questions.explanation: True. Entitlements specify the level of service provided to customers. They define what types of support a customer receives, measured in hours and cases. Entitlements are tied to service contracts and determine service coverage for products and services.

questions.stem: Partner admin contacts have access to the data of both their partner accounts and customer accounts.
questions.explanation: True. Partner admin (sn_customerservice.partner_admin) contacts have access to both their partner accounts and customer accounts. The partner_admin role contains sn_customerservice.partner and sn_customerservice.customer_admin, granting access to manage data for both partner and associated customer accounts.

questions.stem: Which of the following are best practice with regard to data imports? (Choose two.)

options.text: When importing to multiple instances import to each instance separately.
Use ServiceNow automatic functionality to clean the data after it is in ServiceNow tables rather than in the legacy repository.
Ensure the field data lengths in ServiceNow are adequate for the imported data because ServiceNow does not automatically adjust the length.
Images embedded in Knowledge Articles should be uploaded separately.

questions.explanation: Best practices for data imports: Ensure field data lengths in ServiceNow are adequate because the platform does not automatically adjust lengths (C), and images embedded in Knowledge Articles should be uploaded separately (D). Data should be cleaned before import (not after, ruling out B). Import sets can handle multiple instances (ruling out A).

questions.stem: Cost Information on cases is available as part of the Performance Analytics Content Pack for Customer Service.
questions.explanation: False. Cost Information on cases is NOT available as part of the Performance Analytics Content Pack for Customer Service. The PA content pack provides metrics around case volumes, response times, and resolution rates, but cost tracking requires separate configuration or additional modules.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the Guided Decisions capability?

options.text: Provide agents with an escalation guide
Dynamically guide agents to help resolve complex cases
Provide agents with a knowledge guide

questions.explanation: Guided Decisions dynamically guides agents to help resolve complex cases. It provides decision trees with step-by-step questions, answers, and guidance to lead agents through complex case resolution workflows. It's not just an escalation guide (A), account management tool (B), or knowledge guide (D).

questions.stem: Which feature enables you to quickly identify high-priority tasks based on multiple dimensions, not just by a single field value like priority?
questions.explanation: Case Spotlight enables quick identification of high-priority tasks based on multiple dimensions, not just a single field value like priority. It provides a multi-dimensional view of case urgency and importance. Case Performance (A), Analytics (B), and Digest (C) serve different purposes.

questions.stem: During which Now Create stage are workshops conducted?
questions.explanation: Workshops are conducted during the Plan stage of Now Create. The Plan phase involves detailed planning, requirements gathering, and conducting workshops with stakeholders to understand needs and map solutions. Execute (A) is for building, Deliver (C) is deployment, Initiate (B) is project kickoff.

questions.stem: Which application must be activated to enable customers to check in on-line for future appointments?
questions.explanation: Walk-Up Experience must be activated to enable customers to check in online for future appointments. Walk-Up Experience provides a self-service check-in and appointment scheduling capability for in-person support. Business Location (A), FSM (C), and Service Organization (D) don't provide online check-in functionality.

questions.stem: What are some of the influencing factors that will help determine the type of customer support desk structure required? (Choose four.)

options.text: Knowledge and skills required for agents
Number and type of support tools available
Number of customer service portals used

questions.explanation: Influencing factors for support desk structure include: Knowledge and skills required for agents (A), Geographical location of customer (B), Languages spoken by agents (C), and Number of agents required (F). These four directly impact how the desk is structured. Number/type of tools (D) and number of portals (E) are operational details, not structural influencers.

questions.stem: What is the default value in the Channel field when a new case is opened by a customer in the Service Catalog, using the Customer Service Portal?
questions.explanation: The default value in the Channel field when a customer opens a new case from the Service Catalog via the Customer Service Portal is Web. When cases originate from the portal, ServiceNow automatically sets the channel to Web to indicate the source of the case creation.

questions.stem: When activating the Customer Service Management Demo Data plugin, which case type is available besides product case?
questions.explanation: When activating the CSM Demo Data plugin, besides Product case, the Order case type becomes available. These are the two OOB case types provided with demo data. Contract (B), FAQ (C), Monitoring (D), Request (E), and Billing (F) are not OOB case types.

questions.stem: What’s the purpose of the Deactivate Special Handling Notes Scheduled Job?

options.text: Runs at the end of the month and deactivates all Special Handling notes more than 30 days old
Runs weekly and must have the Active checkbox unchecked in order for Special Handling notes to be deleted by the end of the week
Runs on demand by the System Admin who must set specific weekly schedules and set only those that are priority 1-critical to be deactivated
Runs daily at midnight, checks all active alerts and sets the status to Expired for those that have reached their expiration dates

questions.explanation: The Deactivate Special Handling Notes Scheduled Job runs daily at midnight, checks all active alerts, and sets the status to Expired for those that have reached their expiration dates. It doesn't run monthly (A), weekly (B), or on-demand (C). It automates the cleanup of expired SHN records.

questions.stem: What does the Agent Whisper function do?

options.text: Lets agents and chat supervisors have a conversation without the requester knowing
Lets the chat supervisors have a conversation with the requester without the agent knowing
Lets agents have chat conversations with other agents without the requester knowing
Lets agents and requesters have a conversation without the chat supervisor knowing

questions.explanation: Agent Whisper lets agents and chat supervisors have a conversation without the requester knowing. This allows supervisors to provide real-time guidance and coaching to agents during active chat sessions. The requester only sees the agent's messages, not the whisper conversation between agent and supervisor.

questions.stem: Upon self-registration through the Consumer Service Portal, a record is created in: (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Upon self-registration through the Consumer Service Portal, records are created in Consumer User (csm_consumer_user) (B) and Consumer (csm_consumer) (C). The registration creates both a user record and a consumer record. Contact (A) is for B2B customers, and CSM User (D) is not a standard registration table.

questions.stem: Who can create a customer service case from a community discussion? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Customer service agents (sn_customerservice_agent) (A) and Proxy case creators (sn_customerservice.proxy_case_creator) (B) can create cases from community discussions. Partners (C) and Case Viewers (D) don't have the ability to convert community discussions into cases.

questions.stem: The assignment workbench uses configurable matching criteria to evaluate agents in a selected group and provide an overall ranking. What are the different types of criteria available for the assignment workbench? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The assignment workbench criteria types are: Scripted (C), Simple Match (D), and Aggregate (E). These three configurable matching criteria types allow managers to evaluate agents based on different methods — simple field matching, aggregated scores across multiple factors, or custom scripted logic. Correlation (A) and Availability (B) are not criteria types.

questions.stem: Asset classes are defined to allow for logical grouping of assets. There are five asset classes provided to group assets, each Asset class provides unique functionality for that group of Assets in the platform. Which of the following are the asset classes used? (Choose five.)
questions.explanation: The five asset classes are: Hardware assets (A), Facility assets (B), Software licenses assets (D), Enterprise Software assets (E), and Consumables assets (G). These provide logical grouping with unique functionality per class. Configuration assets (C) and Network assets (F) are not standard asset classes in the platform.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes how the CSM application uses the Asset table?

options.text: CSM uses the Product table instead of the ITSM Asset table
CSM uses the Product Model table instead of the ITSM Asset table
ServiceNow uses the same Asset table for both CSM and ITSM, however CSM has a different subset of fields
Because CSM Assets are managed differently from ITSM Assets ServiceNow uses different Asset Tables for CSM than it does for ITSM

questions.explanation: ServiceNow uses the same Asset table for both CSM and ITSM, however CSM has a different subset of fields. The alm_asset table is shared between modules, but CSM surfaces different fields relevant to customer-facing asset tracking (products, services) while ITSM uses fields for lifecycle and financial management.

questions.stem: A consumer service agent receives and accepts a case which was created by a consumer. The agent needs and requests more information from the consumer. After receiving the information, the agent proposes a solution that is accepted by the consumer. Given this scenario, what is the chronological order of case states used to manage this case?

options.text: New > Work in Progress > On Hold > Work in Progress > Resolved > Closed
New > Open > Work in Progress > Solution Proposed > Closed
Open > Pending > Work in Progress > Resolved > Closed
New > Open > Awaiting Info > Open > Resolved > Closed

questions.explanation: The correct chronological order is: New > Open > Awaiting Info > Open > Resolved > Closed. Case starts New, agent accepts (Open), requests more info (Awaiting Info), receives info back (Open), proposes solution (Resolved), customer accepts (Closed). This matches the documented state flow transitions exactly.

questions.stem: What are the types of matching criteria for Customer Service? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The four matching criteria types for Customer Service are: Matching Skills (A), Last Assigned (B), Assigned Cases (E), and Availability Today (F). These evaluate agents based on skills match, recency of assignment, current workload, and current availability. Certifications (C), Distance (D), and Partner Hours (G) are not CSM matching criteria.

questions.stem: What is a supported external customer that, in turn, sells to and supports one or more customers?
questions.explanation: A Partner is a supported external customer that, in turn, sells to and supports one or more customers. Partners are organizations that have been contracted to sell, deliver, and support products/services on behalf of another organization. Account (B) is a direct customer. Contact (C) is a person at an account. Consumer (D) is an individual.

questions.stem: Customer Service Trending Topics is a capability that enables companies to use Predictive Intelligence to quickly pinpoint factors driving up case volume and act to mitigate them. Which of the following would be a benefit of using Predictive Intelligence Customer Service Trending Topics?

options.text: Eliminate the need for more traditional performance analytics
Auto-generate clusters of cases that point to similar underlying issues
Create root cause solutions for similar cases
A guaranteed reduction in call volume per month

questions.explanation: Predictive Intelligence Trending Topics auto-generates clusters of cases that point to similar underlying issues. This benefit allows organizations to quickly identify patterns in case volume drivers. It doesn't eliminate PA (A), create root cause solutions (C), or guarantee call reduction (D).

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow applications can be integrated out-of-the-box with CSM? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: OOB CSM integrations include: Service Portfolio Management (A), Project Management (B), and ITOM Event Management (E). These three have built-in integration points with CSM. DevOps (C) and Risk Management (D) don't have OOB CSM integration.

questions.stem: Which of the following are benefits that may be gained from using communities? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Benefits of communities include: Reduce support costs (A) through case deflection, Engagement with Customers (B) through direct interaction, and Get product feedback (C) from community discussions. Reducing cost per sales (D) and increasing marketing effectiveness (E) are not primary community benefits.

questions.stem: What is a case?

options.text: An individual record that handles and resolves incidents for external customers
An individual record that is used to identify and create automation opportunities
An individual record that is used to identify and resolve a question or issue for an external customer
An individual record that handles and routes issues for internal users

questions.explanation: A case is an individual record used to identify and resolve a question or issue for an external customer. This is the standard CSM definition. Option A limits it to incidents. Option B describes automation. Option D describes ITSM incident management for internal users rather than CSM cases for external customers.

questions.stem: External content integration is important for agents to be able to access knowledge articles from external sources. ALL external sources must be:
questions.explanation: All external sources for knowledge article integration must be WebDAV-compliant. WebDAV (Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning) is the protocol Standard that ServiceNow requires for external content integration. Only applications that support WebDAV connections can integrate their content with ServiceNow knowledge bases.

questions.stem: An Account Relationship is based on a defined account relationship hype. Users with the System Administrator role can define two types of relationships: (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: System Administrators can define two types of account relationships: Account-to-account (C) and Partner-to-account (E). These relationship types allow modeling of business hierarchies and partnerships. Partner-to-customer (A), Account-to-customer (B), and Customer-to-Consumer (D) are not the two defined relationship types.

questions.stem: Which knowledge records can be configured with User Criteria?
questions.explanation: User Criteria can be configured on Knowledge Base and Article records. User criteria provides access control at the knowledge base level and individual article level. Categories (B, C) do not support user criteria configuration. Only Knowledge Bases and Articles have the user criteria capability.

questions.stem: When the virtual agent plugin is installed NLU is activated but is not available for use until what two configurations are completed? (Choose two.)

options.text: In the NLU Settings configure the Intent confidence threshold
In the NLU Settings configure the Entity confidence threshold

questions.explanation: When Virtual Agent plugin is installed, NLU is activated but needs two configurations: Choose the NLU service provider (A) and Enable NLU in Virtual Agent (C). The service provider selection determines which NLU engine processes intents, and it must be explicitly enabled in VA settings. Threshold configurations (B, D) are optional tuning steps.

questions.stem: An entitlement defines the types of support a customer receives. Entitlements are based on a number of standard fields such as product and asset. When Proactive Customer Service Operations is implemented which additional fields could be used? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: With Proactive Customer Service Operations, additional entitlement fields include Install base item (D) and Sold product (E). Standard entitlements use product and asset fields. Proactive CSO extends this with install base item and sold product to enable more granular service-level definitions tied to specific deployed products.

questions.stem: When implementing Knowledge Product Entitlements, what is enabled when activating the Enable access control of Knowledge Articles system property?

options.text: Allows access to knowledge articles based on customer’s security access
Allows access to knowledge articles that are related to entitlements owned by a customer
Allows access to multi-product line knowledge articles
Allows access to knowledge articles that are related to products owned by a customer

questions.explanation: Activating the Knowledge Product Entitlements system property allows access to knowledge articles that are related to products owned by a customer. This restricts knowledge visibility to only those articles associated with products the customer has purchased, providing targeted and relevant content.

questions.stem: Advance Work Assignment assigns work to agents based on their availability, capacity, and skills. Agent Affinity enhances the Advanced Work Assignment process by adding additional agent details organized by affinity type. Which of these are these affinity types? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Agent Affinity types are: Account team responsibility (B), Historical (C), and Related task (D). These enhance AWA by adding context about agent-customer relationships. Account team affinity matches based on team membership, Historical matches based on past interactions, and Related task matches based on connected work items.

questions.stem: In Agent Workspace Chat, Agents have the ability to use quick actions to work more efficiently. What action does the /r quick action perform?

options.text: Rejects an incoming chat and moves it automatically to the “General” queue
Routes the chat towards another group
Uses response templates to insert as text in a conversation
Rolls up the current chat history towards an existing case

questions.explanation: The /r quick action in Agent Workspace Chat uses response templates to insert as text in a conversation. Response templates are pre-configured text snippets that agents can quickly insert into chat conversations for consistent and efficient communication. It doesn't reject chats (A), route them (B), or roll up history (D).

questions.stem: Name a security benefit gained from using scoped applications:

options.text: Prevents changes to tables without explicit permission from IT
Limits accessibility to other applications in the instance
Limits the number of update sets that can be applied

questions.explanation: A security benefit of scoped applications is that it limits accessibility to other applications in the instance. Application scoping creates boundaries between applications so that one app cannot access or modify another app's data or business logic without explicit permission, improving overall instance security.

questions.stem: The CSM application has a feature that can be used to filter records in CSM-related tables which are accessible by users with CSM roles. This feature makes it unnecessary to create business logic for those persona access the data. What is this feature?
questions.explanation: CSM Query Rules filter records in CSM-related tables accessible by users with CSM roles, eliminating the need for custom business logic for persona-based data access. Query rules automatically restrict record visibility based on the user's role, simplifying security configuration.

questions.stem: In Advanced Work Assignment, what does the overflow assignment capability do, if defined?

options.text: When one support group reaches capacity the work item is automatically routed to another group
Uses matching and assignment rules to send work items to the agent with the highest availability
Routes cases to different groups based on their skill set and availability
Uses matching and assignment rules to send work items to the agent with the most capacity

questions.explanation: In AWA, overflow assignment automatically routes work items to another group when one support group reaches capacity. This ensures continuous service delivery even when a primary team is fully loaded. Options B, C, and D describe general AWA routing, not specifically the overflow capability.

questions.stem: Which role must B2B and B2C customers obtain, at a MINIMUM, to access to a ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: The External (snc_external) role is the minimum required for B2B and B2C customers to access a ServiceNow instance. This base role grants the fundamental access needed to interact with the platform. Other CSM-specific roles like customer (C) provide additional capabilities but snc_external is the absolute minimum.

questions.stem: Which Flow Designer flow can be used to automatically close resolved cases if customers do not respond within a specified time?
questions.explanation: The Auto Close Resolved Cases flow in Flow Designer automatically closes resolved cases when customers don't respond within a specified time. This is the OOB mechanism for case auto-closure. The other options (A, C, D) use incorrect naming — the correct name is 'Auto Close Resolved Cases'.

questions.stem: What role can be assigned to employees who are not fulfillers, such as those in sales and services, or do not have other CSM-specific roles, but have a need to create cases on behalf of customers?
questions.explanation: The Proxy Contact (sn_customerservice.proxy_contact) role can be assigned to employees who aren't fulfillers but need to create cases on behalf of customers. This role enables sales, services, or other non-agent staff to submit cases for external customers without requiring full agent capabilities.

questions.stem: Proactive Customer Service Operations works Event Management to proactively monitor and fix issues affecting customers. It can also trigger case workflow’s and enable organizations to notify customers whose services or products are impacted by an outage or issue. What are the three main components that make up Proactive Customer Service Operations? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Proactive Customer Service Operations three main components are: Service-Aware Install Base (B), Proactive Case (D), and Service Monitoring (F). These work together to monitor services, identify impacted customers through install base, and automatically create proactive cases. Options A, C, E are not components of Proactive CSO.

questions.stem: Which roles are considered external? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Customer Admin (sn_customerservice.customer_admin) (B) and Partner Admin (sn_customerservice.partner_admin) (C) are considered external roles. Both contain snc_external and manage accounts from the customer/partner side. Consumer Support Agent (A) and Customer Service Agent (D) are internal fulfiller roles.

questions.stem: The default configuration automatically closes resolved Cases after how many days?

options.text: Cases are not automatically closed by default

questions.explanation: Cases are NOT automatically closed by default. While the Auto Close Resolved Cases flow exists, it is not enabled by default. Administrators must explicitly activate and configure it. The other options (5 days, 3 days, 10 days) are all incorrect.

questions.stem: What do blue circles in the timeline of a case form represent?
questions.explanation: Blue circles in the timeline of a case form represent State changes. The timeline uses blue circle indicators to mark when the case transitions between states (New, Open, Awaiting Info, Resolved, Closed). Triggered SLAs (A), Activity updates (B), and Customer comments (C) use different visual indicators.

questions.stem: What are the different resource matching methods on the Matching Rule form? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The four resource matching methods on the Matching Rule form are: Scripted (B), Advanced (C), Simple (D), and Selection Criteria (F). These methods determine how matching rules evaluate agents against case requirements. History (A) and Skill (E) are matching criteria, not matching methods.

questions.stem: Which of the following child case states would cause parent - child case synchronization to fail? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Child case states that cause parent-child synchronization to fail are: Resolved (A), Closed (E), and Cancelled (F). Synchronization cannot update child cases in these terminal states because they've reached a final resolution. In Progress (B), Awaiting Info (C), and New (D) are active states that allow synchronization.

questions.stem: External customers can view the problem, change, and request records associated with their customer service cases from the Customer and Consumer Service Portals. Which of the following can they approve in relation to cases via the portals?
questions.explanation: External customers can approve Change Records and Request Records via the Customer and Consumer Service Portals. These portals allow customers to view and approve changes and requests associated with their cases. Problem records (C, D) and escalations (A) don't have OOB portal approval capabilities.

questions.stem: Playbooks for CSM provide step-by-step guidance for resolving specific types of customer service cases. What are the three out-of-the-box playbooks for CSM? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three OOB playbooks for CSM are: Case playbook for Onboarding (A), Case playbook for Product Support (C), and Case playbook for Complaints (D). These provide step-by-step guidance for the most common CSM case scenarios. Services (B) and Billing (E) are not OOB playbook types.

questions.stem: Based on which out-of-box attributes can Special handling Notes be applied to cases? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Out-of-box, Special Handling Notes can be applied based on: Product (C), Account (D), and Contact (E). These three entity types are the OOB attributes for SHN on cases. Service Contract (A) and Install Base Item (B) are not OOB SHN attributes.

questions.stem: As an agent you can report a knowledge gap, if you cannot find relevant articles that could help resolve a case. Which action is required to create the knowledge gap?

options.text: Document the knowledge gap in the case work notes and escalate the case
Post a question in one of the various Customer Service Management knowledge bases
Use Related Links on the case form to report a knowledge gap
Use the Create Knowledge button on the case form to report a knowledge gap

questions.explanation: To report a knowledge gap, use Related Links on the case form to report a knowledge gap. This built-in feature allows agents to flag missing knowledge directly from the case context, creating a knowledge gap record. work notes (A), community posting (B), and Create Knowledge button (D) are not the gap reporting mechanism.

questions.stem: What feature does the Product Model and Catalog Items Relationship plugin enable?

options.text: Agents are automatically proposed catalog items related to the chosen product on the case form
Consumers can track what products they have purchased via the catalog
It provides a contextual service catalog based on the customer’s subscribed services
Customer service managers can track the financial cost of customer’s subscribed services and the related requests

questions.explanation: The Product Model and Catalog Items Relationship plugin provides a contextual service catalog based on the customer's subscribed services. This enables the catalog to display only relevant items based on what products/services the customer has, creating a personalized catalog experience rather than showing all items.

questions.stem: What happens to a case whenever the state of one of the associated IT Service Management records (incident, problem, change) is updated?

options.text: The case escalates to an assignment group as defined in the default escalation template
The case work notes are updated automatically
The case action status changes to Related Task Updated
The case displays a special handling note highlighting the update

questions.explanation: When the state of an associated ITSM record (incident, problem, change) is updated, the case work notes are updated automatically. This automatic work note update keeps the case record current with progress from related ITSM activities. The case doesn't escalate (A), change action status (C), or display SHN (D) for ITSM updates.

questions.stem: Application Scoping from a security perspective brings the following benefits: (Choose two.)

options.text: Improves instance security by limiting access to other applications on the instance
Scoped applications prevent versioning for complex instances
Scoping hold the records and acts as a container for the desired CSM applications
Scoped applications limits autonomy and control of all aspects of the CSM application

questions.explanation: Application scoping security benefits: Improves instance security by limiting access to other applications (A), and Scoping holds records and acts as a container for CSM applications (C). Scoping doesn't prevent versioning (B), and it provides autonomy and control rather than limiting it (D).

questions.stem: How can multiple service catalogs be made available on the Customer Service Portal?

options.text: Include them in the list of service catalogs on the Customer Service Portal record
Add them to the list of service catalogs in the Customer Service Portal header widget options
Only the Customer Service service catalog can be used on the Customer Service Portal
Create user criteria for each of the applicable service catalogs

questions.explanation: Include multiple service catalogs in the list of service catalogs on the Customer Service Portal record. The portal configuration allows specifying which catalogs are available, enabling multiple catalogs to be presented. It's not limited to header widget options (B), a single catalog (C), or user criteria (D).

questions.stem: Now Create provides a prescriptive methodology, leading practices, and accelerators to help with ServiceNow implementations and upgrades. How many sequential project phases and exit gates are there in the Now Create Methodology?
questions.explanation: Now Create methodology has Five sequential project phases and exit gates. The five phases are: Initiate, Plan, Execute, Deliver, and Close. Each phase has defined exit gates that must be met before progressing. Three (A), Four (C), and Six (D) are incorrect counts.

questions.stem: From which one of the following can an agent create a CSM Case:
questions.explanation: An agent can create a CSM Case from Chat. Chat interactions with customers can be converted into cases directly. Human Resource Application (A) is a separate module. Incident Management (B) creates incidents, not cases. Special Handling Note (D) is informational and doesn't create cases.

questions.stem: Using the out-of-the-box major issue management process flow, a consumer service agent proposes an existing case in the Open state as a major case candidate. The major case candidate has a consumer defined and is approved by the customer service manager What happens to the major case candidate?

options.text: The major case candidate becomes a major case
A new major case is created and the major case candidate is added as a child to the major case
The major case candidate requires an approval from the major issue manager
The major case candidate is closed and a new major case is created

questions.explanation: A new major case is created and the major case candidate is added as a child to the major case. When a case is proposed and approved as a major case candidate, the system creates a separate major case record and links the original case as a child. The candidate doesn't become the major case itself (A) and isn't closed (D).

questions.stem: What types of escalation templates can be created? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Escalation template types that can be created are: Case (A) and Account (D). These two escalation template types cover the primary CSM escalation scenarios — escalating individual cases or entire accounts. Sold Product (B) and Consumer (C) don't have dedicated escalation templates.

questions.stem: What are the recommended good practices when running implementation workshops? (Choose three.)

options.text: Give the customers the data they need so they can make an informed decision
Any financial implication of a decision should be handled by the delivery and sales team
Enforce customers to adapt their processes towards the baseline processes
Engage with customers to gain deep understanding of their organization
Guide the customer toward industry best practices

questions.explanation: Good practices for workshops: Give customers data for informed decisions (A), Engage deeply to understand their organization (D), and Guide toward industry best practices (E). Financial implications should be handled transparently (not separately, ruling out B). Don't enforce process adaptation (C) — guide instead.

questions.stem: What is the specific type of catalog item called that allows users to create task-based records, such as case records, from the Service Catalog?
questions.explanation: A Record Producer is the specific catalog item type that allows users to create task-based records like case records from the Service Catalog. Record Producers generate records on any table, making them ideal for case creation from the catalog. Request Item (A), Catalog Processor (C), and Case Template (D) serve different purposes.

questions.stem: Out-of-box, which functionality handles state transitioning for case management?
questions.explanation: Out-of-box, State Flows handle state transitioning for case management. State flows define the valid state transitions and actions available at each state. Workflows (A), Business Rules (C), and Flows (D) can influence behavior but state transitioning is handled by State Flows in CSM.

questions.stem: Which of the following are benefits of customer access management? (Choose two.)

options.text: It defaults the responsibility for access management to the customer service agent.
It increases security by automatically providing access to case information based on account hierarchy
It increases automation by automatically granting access to cases based on access to sold product
It improves the customer experience by enabling related parties to track and collaborate on cases.
It defaults the responsibility for access management to the customer.

questions.explanation: Benefits of customer access management: Increases automation by automatically granting access to cases based on access to sold product (C), and Improves customer experience by enabling related parties to track and collaborate on cases (D). It doesn't default to agent responsibility (A) or auto-provide based on hierarchy alone (B).

questions.stem: What are the advantages of leading indicators over lagging indicators? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Leading indicators advantages over lagging: Prospective (B) — they look forward and predict future outcomes, and Easy to influence (D) — actions can be taken to change them. Lagging indicators are retrospective (C) and hard to influence (A) since they measure past events.

questions.stem: Customer Service Management Administrators can delegate Contact Administration activities to specific contacts within accounts by assigning specific roles to one or more users. Which of the following roles, if assigned, would allow the user to create contacts?
questions.explanation: The customer_admin (sn_customerservice.customer_admin) role allows the user to create contacts. This role includes admin capabilities for the customer account, including contact management. Customer case manager (A), account manager (B), and base customer (D) roles don't include contact creation permissions.

questions.stem: What is knowledge article versioning?

options.text: A content tracker for knowledge articles
The ability to manage and track article updates

questions.explanation: Knowledge article versioning is the ability to manage and track article updates. It enables knowledge managers to maintain multiple versions of articles, track changes over time, and control which version is published. It's not a content tracker (A), publishing guide (B), or numbering guide (D).

questions.stem: Service providers use business models to support their various customers. What type of customer is supported with the Business-to-Consumer (B2C) model?
questions.explanation: Business-to-Consumer (B2C) supports Individuals as customers. In B2C, the service provider deals directly with individual people (consumers) rather than through business accounts. Partners (B) are B2B entities. Contacts (C) are B2B employees. Accounts (D) represent businesses in B2B.

questions.stem: When configuring email in Communication Channels, how many outgoing email addresses are supported?
questions.explanation: Only one outgoing email address is supported when configuring email in CSM Communication Channels. CSM supports a single outbound email configuration for case correspondence. Multiple outbound addresses (B, C, D) are not supported out of the box.

questions.stem: Which of the following roles have permission to create a relationship between a contact and an account? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The sn_customerservice_manager (D) and admin (E) roles can create relationships between contacts and accounts. The manager role includes the permissions needed for contact-account relationship management, and the admin role has full system access. Agent (A), customer_admin (B/C), and partner_admin (C) don't have this specific permission.

questions.stem: In CSM Asset Management has a different meaning than in ITSM or Corporate Finance Which of the following defines Asset Management in CSM?

options.text: The process of developing, operating, maintaining, upgrading, and disposing of assets in me most cost-effective manner
A generic activity or process responsible for tracking and reporting the value and ownership of assets throughout their lifecycle
Asset management has different use cases for tracking specific products or services customers are using
It includes all of the data crucial to support customers as efficiently as possible

questions.explanation: In CSM, Asset Management means tracking specific products or services customers are using. Unlike ITSM's cost-effective lifecycle management (A) or corporate finance tracking (B), CSM focuses on understanding what products a customer has deployed so agents can provide targeted support. Option D is too broad.

questions.stem: What is KCS (Knowledge Centered Services)?

options.text: A bunch of tables strictly pertaining to CSM case articles that focus on mapping articles to Knowledge management
A documented methodology to provide a set of best practices for creating and maintaining knowledge
A dashboard with specific visualization of the different knowledge bases and categories
An application that helps agents and managers to create cases from Knowledge articles

questions.explanation: KCS (Knowledge Centered Services) is a documented methodology providing best practices for creating and maintaining knowledge. It defines processes for capturing, structuring, reusing, and improving knowledge articles. It's not tables (A), a dashboard (C), or a case creation app (D).

questions.stem: When creating or importing assets for CSM, model categories are used to: (Choose three.)

options.text: Define whether a Configuration Item (CI) is created when an Asset record is created or vice versa
Build a classification structure for product models
Model the configuration options for each product model being sold to customers
Define a link between Asset classes and Configuration Item (CI) classes

questions.explanation: Model categories are used to: Define whether a CI is created when an Asset record is created or vice versa (A), Group assets together (B), and Define a link between Asset classes and CI classes (E). They don't build classification for product models (C) or model configuration options (D).

questions.stem: Viewing a customer’s install base in the CSM Workspaces enables customer service agents to: (Choose two.)

options.text: Close an upsell of related products and services not yet purchased by a customer
See the detailed configurations of the products and services deployed for a customer to determine the action needed
Trace Information provided in a case to the right product or service to which it relates
Monitor related operational services and configuration items that affect service health

questions.explanation: Viewing a customer's install base enables agents to: Close an upsell of related products not yet purchased (A) and See detailed configurations to determine action needed (B). The install base view shows what the customer has and identifies gaps for upselling, plus provides configuration details for troubleshooting. Options C and D describe different capabilities.

questions.stem: Benefits of Proactive Customer Service Operations include: (Choose two.)

options.text: Major cases can be eliminated as there will be no Impact to customers

questions.explanation: Proactive CSO benefits include: Reduced inbound calls from customers (A) and Reduced Mean Time To Resolve (D). By proactively notifying customers of issues, fewer customers need to call in. Proactive identification speeds resolution. Staff turnover (B) isn't directly impacted, issues can't be eliminated (C), and satisfaction isn't guaranteed (E).

questions.stem: What features are included with the Customer Service Portal? (Choose three.)

options.text: Header with links for different customer activities such as creating a case
Search feature to get information from several repositories
Links to information sources such as the knowledge base, community and customer support
Links to marketing promotions and product coupons
The ability to create new accounts

questions.explanation: Customer Service Portal features include: Header with links for activities like case creation (A), Search feature for multiple repositories (B), and Links to knowledge base, community, and support (C). Marketing promotions (D) and account creation (E) are not standard portal features.

questions.stem: What does NLU stand for?
questions.explanation: NLU stands for Natural-Language Understanding. It's the AI technology that enables Virtual Agent to interpret user intent from natural language input. The other options (Natural-Learning Userability, Natural-Learning URL, Natural-Language URL) are fabricated terms.

questions.stem: Out-of-the-box. cases are automatically closed after how many days?

options.text: Cases are not automatically closed by default

questions.explanation: Cases are not automatically closed by default in the OOB configuration. The Auto Close Resolved Cases flow exists but must be explicitly activated and configured. The 3-day (A), 5-day (B), and 10-day (C) options are all incorrect — there is no default auto-close timer enabled.

questions.stem: When are any changes to the platform considered a customization?

options.text: When they require an implementation spread across all project phases
If they are NOT applied through the usage of built-in tools on the Now Platform
When they are solely implemented for a custom application
When there are business demands for custom functionality that is not offered out-of-the-box

questions.explanation: Changes to the platform are considered customization when there are business demands for custom functionality not offered out-of-the-box. Customization means implementing features beyond what the platform provides natively. Configuration using built-in tools is not customization. Options A, B, C don't correctly define the customization boundary.

questions.stem: Which solution must be implemented to let a breakdown dashboard appear as a pop-up window on the case form?
questions.explanation: In-form Analytics is the solution that enables a breakdown dashboard to appear as a pop-up window on the case form. It embeds Performance Analytics visualizations directly within the form context. Service Analytics (A), Case Spotlight (C), and Prediction Results (D) don't provide in-form pop-up dashboard functionality.

questions.stem: The case digests feature includes which types of case communication? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Case digests feature includes Case Action Summaries (B) and Post Case Reviews (C). These two communication types allow stakeholders to receive summaries of case activities and post-resolution reviews. Case Lifecycle Reports (A) and Case Post Mortem (D) are not part of the case digests feature.

questions.stem: By default what can customers with the customer (sn_customerservice.customer) role see on the customer service portal? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: By default, customers with the sn_customerservice.customer role can see on the portal: Assets (A), Publications (B), and Products (C). These are visible in the customer's default portal view. Contacts (D) and Contracts (E) require additional permissions or roles to be visible.

questions.stem: Which feature allows an agent to copy reusable messages to case or task forms to provide quick and consistent messages to users?
questions.explanation: Response Templates allow agents to copy reusable messages to case or task forms for quick and consistent communication. They are pre-configured text blocks that can be inserted into records. Quick Messages (A), Quick Actions (B), and Templates (D) are either different features or don't specifically serve this purpose.

questions.stem: In the Customer Service Management space what defines the term asset?

options.text: A specific product instance supported for a customer
A product that a company supports
A resource that allows a business service

questions.explanation: In CSM, an asset is a specific product instance supported for a customer. This distinguishes CSM's customer-centric view from ITSM's internal lifecycle view. It's not just a physical item (A), not a general product model (C), and not a business service resource (D). It represents the specific deployed instance of a product for a customer.

questions.stem: Which capabilities does the integration with Microsoft Outlook add-in offer? (Choose two.)

options.text: Escalate a case on the add-m panel of Outlook
Register the sender of an email as contact
As the Microsoft Outlook user, register yourself as self-contributor
Create cases using email content in Outlook for the customer contact

questions.explanation: Microsoft Outlook add-in capabilities: Register the sender of an email as contact (B) and Create cases using email content in Outlook for the customer contact (D). These enable agents to manage CSM workflows directly from Outlook. Escalating cases (A) and self-registration as contributor (C) are not add-in features.

questions.stem: To which entities can Special Handling Notes be applied out of the box?
questions.explanation: Consumer is an entity to which Special Handling Notes can be applied out of the box. The OOB SHN entities are Contact, Account, Product, and Consumer. Entitlement (B) and Sold Product (C) are not OOB entities for Special Handling Notes.

questions.stem: Which service catalogs are available out-of-the-box in the customer portals? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The OOB service catalogs available in customer portals are Customer Service (B) and Consumer Service (C). The Customer Service catalog serves B2B portal users and Consumer Service serves B2C consumers. Partner Service (A) and Product Service (D) are not OOB catalog types.

questions.stem: Partner admin (sn_customerservice.partner_admin) contacts have access to:
questions.explanation: Partner admin contacts have access to Both their partner accounts and customer accounts. The partner_admin role contains both the partner and customer_admin roles, enabling full access to data from both partner and customer perspectives, allowing them to manage users and cases across both.

questions.stem: From a security perspective, scoping brings several benefits: (Choose two.)

options.text: Improves instance security by limiting accessibility to other applications on the instance
Provides CSM teams the autonomy and control needed to configure and manage the CSM application, but not the CSM Service Portals
IT can manage and control the pace of the CSM teams because dependencies have been put in place
The scope holds the records and acts as a container for the desired Customer Service Management Applications

questions.explanation: Security benefits of scoping: Improves instance security by limiting accessibility to other applications (A), and The scope holds records and acts as a container for CSM Applications (D). Scoping provides autonomy for all CSM including portals (ruling out B), and eliminates dependencies rather than creating them (ruling out C).

questions.stem: Advanced Work Assignment (AWA) pushes work to qualified agents using work item queues, routing conditions, and assignment criteria that you define. Which step would ensure the work was allocated to the appropriate agent?

options.text: Set the Agent Experience (What agents see in their Workspace inbox)
Define Assignment Rules (How to assign work items)
Define Work Item Queues (Where to route)

questions.explanation: Define Assignment Rules ensures work is allocated to the appropriate agent in AWA. This step configures the criteria for routing work items to the right agents based on skills, availability, and capacity. Agent Experience (A) is about agent UI. Work Item Queues (C) is about routing destinations. Service Channels (D) is about what to route.
